idiom_name: node:fs spool (writeFile + FileHandle.sync + rename) drained by an async loop
implementation_notes: Node supplies the primitives but no durable queue: open a temp file in the spool directory, write the payload (the writeFile/appendFile flush option, Node 21+, or an explicit FileHandle.sync() flushes it to the storage device), close it and rename it into the spool, then drain with a single async loop that deletes a file only after the peer acknowledged. Broker clients cover the hop only - an amqplib ConfirmChannel invokes the publish callback once the broker confirmed the message and waitForConfirms() gives the same barrier - and an in-process array or promise chain is not a store at all. Move the drain loop into a worker thread or a separate process when fsync latency must not block request handling.
pitfalls: fs.writeFile resolving means the data reached the kernel, not the disk: without sync()/flush a spool entry can be lost in a crash.
fs.rename across devices throws EXDEV - the temporary file must live in the spool directory.
An interval-driven drain overlaps itself when a pass runs long; guard it with a single in-flight flag or serialize the passes.
Unhandled 'error' events on a channel or connection crash the process (amqplib documents this) and take the undrained spool down with it - reconnection and backpressure must be explicit.
